paras: The whipping of William Perkins was an attack on a Black man at Hulbert, Arkansas, reported in a dispatch dated June 27, 1919, in which a group of white men seized him, carried him to the swamps and lashed him. According to the report, he was punished for telling people how well Black people were treated in Chicago, and several other people were ordered to leave the town. The Chicago Defender carried the story on its front page under a headline calling it a murder, although its text describes a beating followed by a trip to the hospital.

The Defender's correspondent wrote that Perkins had told people at Hulbert how well "his Race was treated in Chicago, Ill." In response a group, whose description is garbled in the surviving text, seized him, carried him to the swamps and "applied lashes to his back." The report said that after the beating his "incarcerated" (probably "lacerated") body was taken to the hospital.

A few white men were then said to have come out of the woods, and one of them reportedly declared, "He'll never tell any nigger again about how darkies are treated up here." Perkins, the paper added, "was not the only one to feel the cruel hand of the whites," as several other people were ordered to leave town.
No report of arrests, an inquest or any official response appears in the coverage, and nothing further was found on Perkins's condition or on those ordered out.

The episode appears in the Black press only as a short front-page item in the Chicago Defender of June 28, 1919, printed among other brief dispatches from the South. The Defender's headline, "Murder Man Who Told," framed the attack as a killing and as retaliation for news of Chicago, a theme the paper stressed by quoting the white man's boast. The item closed with a garbled remark that the town would not permit members of the Race to wear war decorations.
Whether Perkins survived is unclear from the single report: its headline speaks of murder, while its text describes a whipping after which he was taken to the hospital.

accounts.label: Black correspondent (Hulbert dispatch)
accounts.gist: Perkins was seized, taken to the swamps and whipped because he praised conditions for Black people in Chicago; a white man was quoted saying he would never tell 'any nigger again' about it, and several others were ordered out of town.

framing.detail: The Chicago Defender ran the item on page one under 'Murder Man Who Told', spoke of 'the cruel hand of the whites' and linked the attack to talk of Chicago.

versions.value: Killed: the headline reads 'Murder Man Who Told'
Beaten and taken to the hospital, per the body text

conflicts.note: Both versions are in the same article. The body text is more specific, but the OCR is garbled ('incarcerated body', likely 'lacerated'), and no follow-up was found to settle whether Perkins survived.
